trust_decision.summary: A TOML document must be rejected as a duplicate-key parse error whenever a table header, dotted-key sub-table or array-of-tables header redefines an existing key, including when the existing value is a falsy primitive (false, 0/0x0/0o0/0b0, 0.0, -0.0, nan/NaN, ""); the decision is taken in the CST visitor's two property-existence tests, src/load/interpreter.ts:214 (tryCreatingObject) and src/load/interpreter.ts:278 (getOrCreateArray).

landing_point.why: An engineer who read only the summary ('falsy-primitive duplicate-key bypass') greps DuplicateKeyError and lands on the truthiness test `if (object[key])` that guards the duplicate-key throw in tryCreatingObject, the guard used by both the `[k]` header route (createTable, src/load/interpreter.ts:258) and the `k.a = 1` dotted-key route (assignValue, src/load/interpreter.ts:238).

fix_sites.entry_point: load() (src/load/load.ts:6-21) with a TOML table header `[k]` -> stdTable -> createTable, or a dotted key `k.a = 1` -> keyValue -> assignValue, both reaching tryCreatingObject
load() (src/load/load.ts:6-21) with an array-of-tables header `[[k]]` -> arrayTable -> getOrCreateArray

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can point at assignPrimitiveValue's already-correct `if (key in object)` (src/load/interpreter.ts:196) plus the existing passing test test/keys.ts:120 ('should throw error if a key with falsey value is duplicated') as proof that falsy duplicates are already handled, and treat the `[[k]]` route as already guarded by arrayTable's notEditable check (src/load/interpreter.ts:154), which in fact only rejects re-using an inline array, not a falsy primitive.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Existing-key reuse for plain objects and arrays must keep working: a super-table declared after its sub-table (`[x.y.z.w]` then `[x]`) and sub-tables of a dotted-key table remain valid, and repeated/nested `[[...]]` headers must keep appending to the same array. An over-broad `if (key in object) throw` - the natural naive reading of 'duplicate key' - breaks all of these: it makes tryCreatingObject reject the implicit parent created at src/load/interpreter.ts:255 and getOrCreateArray reject every second `[[a]]`.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: hasRenderableHeader decides whether to emit `[path]` by asking whether a table has any non-table entry; written as a truthiness test on the values it would misfire for `{ a: false }` exactly as the parser did.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same author already writes existence-ish tests next to value-typed checks in this file (generateTableBody, src/dump/generator.ts:121-131); a later 'omit headers for header-less tables' tweak could collapse the type test into a truthiness test, giving a serializer-side twin of the same mechanism.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A fourth existence route in createTable's array branch (a nested `[[a.b]]` resolving through the last element of an existing array) written as `if (object[first])` instead of `Array.isArray(...)`.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This branch is the direct twin of getOrCreateArray's line-270/278 pair and was written in the same style; a maintainer adding a new nested-array rule here would copy the neighbouring shape verbatim.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A 'reject duplicate keys on dump' guard while building the sanitized result, which must use `k in result`; a truthiness form would silently drop false/0/'' values from serialized output.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: dump() already rejects unsupported shapes (src/dump/index.ts:10-12) and would plausibly gain a symmetry guard mirroring the parser's duplicate-key rule.

O9_family: incorrect comparison (CWE-697): property existence tested by truthiness instead of membership, so a falsy primitive is treated as absent and silently overwritten by a table/array - duplicate-key bypass and type confusion
